newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - March 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - March 7.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page Friday:

* A swaying 70-foot maple toppled by high winds crushed a church van filled with children headed to school, killing four girls and injuring six others in the Jamaica section of New York City's Queens borough.

* In the first signficant revision of its national criminal code since 1979, China elimated the category of "counterrevolutionary" crimes and added new offenses such as insider trading and money laundering.

* Republicans pushed through approval of $4.4 million to fund an investigation of illegal campaign activities in the 1996 elections. Meanwhile, the new general chairman of the Democratic National Committee, Colorado Gov. Roy Romer, criticized the acceptance of a $50,000 campaign donation by Hillary Rodham Clinton's chief of staff in 1995.

* U.S. immigration officials say the backlog of applications for citizenship has grown so large that many immigrants are unlikely to meet an August deadline for citizenship, thereby losing their welfare benefits.
* Advertising by liquor and beer companies and tobacco companies on the World Wide Web is drawing criticism from children's advocates such as the National Parent Teachers Association.

* The owner of a Miami strip parlor named Porky's is in jail following a plot to buy a Russian submarine for cocaine-smuggling, raising law enforcement concerns that a new wave of Russian mobsters is infiltrating the Miami vice scene.
